questions.question: Quick Add: What is 15 + 12?
questions.explanation: 15 + 10 = 25, plus 2 more equals 27!

questions.question: Calendar Quickie: If today is Tuesday, what day of the week will it be tomorrow?
questions.explanation: The day directly after Tuesday is Wednesday.
questions.hintText: Monday, Tuesday, ...?

questions.question: Everyday Science: At what temperature (in °C) does liquid water boil into steam at sea level?
questions.explanation: Water freezes at 0 °C and boils at 100 °C at standard atmospheric pressure.
questions.hintText: 0 °C is freezing; 100 °C is boiling!

questions.question: 1-Move Capture (White to move): Find the winning move to capture Black's undefended piece!
questions.explanation: 1. Rxd5 wins Black's Queen for free along the open d-file!
questions.hintText: Move your White Rook straight up from d1 to d5 to capture the Black Queen!

questions.question: Quick Synonym: Which word means the SAME as 'HAPPY'?
questions.explanation: 'Joyful' means full of happiness and delight.
questions.hintText: Joy = happiness!

questions.question: Quick Code: What number does print(5 + 5) show on the screen?
questions.explanation: 5 + 5 adds the two numbers together and prints 10.
questions.hintText: 5 plus 5 equals 10.

questions.question: Quick Add: What is 25 + 35?
Sequence: 2, 4, 8, 16, ... What comes next?
questions.explanation: Powers of 2: 16 x 2 = 32.
questions.hintText: Double each number.

questions.question: Space Fact: What is the brightest star seen from Earth during the day?
questions.explanation: The Sun is the closest star to Earth.
questions.hintText: It lights up our day!

questions.question: Synonym: What is a synonym for 'tiny'?
questions.explanation: Tiny means very small.
questions.hintText: Think of a tiny insect.

questions.question: Chess Pieces: Which piece can move backward, forward, and sideways any number of squares?
questions.explanation: The Rook moves horizontally and vertically any distance.
questions.hintText: The castle tower piece.

questions.question: Code Output: In Python, what is len('Cat')?
questions.explanation: 'Cat' has 3 characters: C, a, t.
questions.hintText: Count the letters in Cat.

questions.question: Mental Math: What is 12 x 5?
Riddle: If you have 3 apples and take away 2, how many do you have?
questions.explanation: You took 2 apples, so you have 2 apples!
questions.hintText: Read carefully: how many do YOU have?

questions.question: Energy: What kind of energy does a moving car possess?
questions.explanation: Kinetic energy is energy of motion.
questions.hintText: Kinetic means related to motion.

questions.question: Antonym: What is the opposite of 'Victory'?
questions.explanation: Defeat is the opposite of victory.
questions.hintText: The opposite of winning.

questions.question: Division: What is 48 / 6?
questions.hintText: Count by 6s up to 48.

questions.question: Pawn Promotion: What can a pawn promote to when reaching the 8th rank?
questions.explanation: A pawn can promote to a Queen, Rook, Bishop, or Knight.
questions.hintText: Most players choose a Queen!

questions.question: Syntax: Which symbol is used for comments in Python?
questions.explanation: # denotes a single-line comment in Python.
questions.hintText: Hash / pound key.

questions.question: Compass: If you face North and turn 90 degrees clockwise, which way do you face?
questions.explanation: Turning clockwise from North points to East.
questions.hintText: North, East, South, West.

questions.question: Sound: Can sound travel through a vacuum (empty space)?
questions.optionsString: Yes|No|Only in zero gravity|Faster than in air
questions.explanation: Sound requires a medium (air, water, solid) to vibrate.
questions.hintText: In space, no one can hear you scream!

questions.question: Squares: What is 9 squared (9 x 9)?
questions.hintText: Think 9 x 10 = 90, minus 9 = 81.

questions.question: Compound Words: Which of these is a compound word?
questions.explanation: Sun + light = Sunlight.
questions.hintText: Two words combined into one.

questions.question: Checkmate: What is it called when the King is attacked and has no legal moves?
questions.explanation: Checkmate ends the game with a win for the attacker.
questions.hintText: The ultimate goal in chess.

questions.question: Data Structures: In code, what is an ordered collection of items called?
questions.explanation: A list (or array) stores ordered elements.
questions.hintText: [item1, item2, item3]

questions.question: Perimeter: A square has sides of 5 cm. What is its perimeter?
questions.explanation: Perimeter = 4 x 5 cm = 20 cm.
questions.hintText: Add all 4 sides.

questions.question: Odd One: Which one is NOT a mammal?
questions.explanation: An eagle is a bird, while dolphins and whales are mammals.
questions.hintText: Lays hard-shelled eggs.

questions.question: Heat Transfer: How does heat travel from the Sun to Earth across space?
questions.explanation: Electromagnetic radiation travels through empty vacuum.
questions.hintText: Infrared light waves.

questions.question: Spelling: Which word is spelled correctly?
questions.explanation: 'Definitely' is the correct spelling.
questions.hintText: Root word: finite.

questions.question: Percentages: What is 50% of 84?
questions.hintText: Divide 84 by 2.

questions.question: Castling: Which two pieces participate in castling?
questions.optionsString: King and Queen|King and Rook|Bishop and Knight|Rook and Pawn
questions.explanation: Castling is a special move involving King and Rook.
questions.hintText: King moves 2 squares toward the Rook.

questions.question: Operators: What does the % (modulo) operator calculate?
questions.explanation: Modulo returns the remainder (e.g. 7 % 3 = 1).
questions.hintText: Remainder after integer division.

questions.question: Time: How many seconds are in 3 minutes?
questions.explanation: 3 x 60 = 180 seconds.
questions.hintText: 60 seconds in 1 minute.

packs.title: Tweens & Middle School (10–13 yrs): Smart STEM & Logic
packs.subtitle: Grades 5–8 percentages, speed & distance, solar eclipses, sequences & Python loops
packs.author: QuizLock STEM Academy

questions.question: Percentage Quarter: What is 25% (one quarter) of 100?
Speed & Distance: A train travels at a steady speed of 60 km/h for 2 hours. How many kilometers does it travel?
questions.explanation: Distance d = v × t = 60 km/h × 2 h = 120 km.
questions.hintText: Multiply speed (60) × time (2).

questions.question: Pattern Detective: What number comes next in the doubling sequence: 3, 6, 12, 24, ...?
questions.hintText: Double 24 (24 × 2).

questions.question: Space Science: What causes a Solar Eclipse on Earth?
questions.optionsString: The Moon passes between the Sun and Earth|Earth passes into Mars's shadow|The Sun turns off briefly|Clouds block the sky
questions.explanation: A solar eclipse happens when the Moon moves directly between the Sun and Earth, casting a shadow on Earth.
questions.hintText: Which celestial body blocks the Sun's light during a solar eclipse?

questions.question: Word Power: What does the adjective 'BENEVOLENT' mean?
questions.optionsString: Kind and well-meaning|Extremely loud|Hostile and angry|Freezing cold
questions.explanation: From Latin 'bene' (well/good), 'benevolent' means kind, generous, and well-meaning.
questions.hintText: Latin root 'bene' means good or well.

questions.question: Python Loop Counter: How many times does the loop `for i in range(5):` repeat?
questions.explanation: range(5) generates the 5 integers 0, 1, 2, 3, 4 — so the loop runs exactly 5 times.
questions.hintText: Count the numbers 0, 1, 2, 3, 4.

questions.question: Fractions: What is 3/4 + 1/8 expressed in eighths?
questions.explanation: Convert to common denominator: 3/4 = 6/8. Then 6/8 + 1/8 = 7/8.
questions.hintText: Multiply the numerator and denominator of 3/4 by 2 to get eighths.

questions.question: Earth Science: Which layer of the Earth lies directly beneath the crust?
questions.explanation: The mantle is the thick silicate rock layer situated between Earth's crust and outer core.
questions.hintText: It makes up about 84% of Earth's total volume.

questions.question: Geometry: What is the sum of the three interior angles of ANY triangle on a flat plane?
questions.explanation: On a flat Euclidean plane, the interior angles of any triangle always sum to 180°.
questions.hintText: If you tear off the three corners of a paper triangle, they form a straight line (180°).

questions.question: Python Basics: What is the zero-based index of the FIRST element in any Python list?
questions.explanation: In Python and most modern programming languages, array and list indexing starts at index 0.
questions.hintText: Computer science counting begins at zero!

questions.question: States of Matter: What is the scientific term when a solid turns directly into a gas without melting into liquid first?
questions.explanation: Sublimation is the phase transition directly from solid to gas (like dry ice solid CO₂).
questions.hintText: Think of dry ice turning directly into smoke-like gas at room temperature.

questions.question: Ratios & Scale: A model car has a scale ratio of 1:10. If the real car is 250 cm long, how long is the model car?
questions.explanation: Scale 1:10 means divide by 10: 250 cm / 10 = 25 cm.
questions.hintText: Divide the real length (250 cm) by 10.

questions.question: Life Sciences: Which cellular organelle is often called the 'powerhouse of the cell' for producing ATP energy?
questions.explanation: Mitochondria generate most of the chemical energy (ATP) needed to power cell reactions.
questions.hintText: Starts with 'M' and fuels your muscle cells.

questions.question: Algebraic Thinking: If 3x + 5 = 20, what is the value of 2x + 25?
questions.hintText: First solve for x by subtracting 5 from 20, then dividing by 3.

questions.question: Density: An object has a mass of 60 grams and a volume of 20 cm³. What is its density?
questions.explanation: Density = Mass / Volume = 60 g / 20 cm³ = 3 g/cm³.
questions.hintText: Divide mass by volume (60 / 20).

questions.question: Python Slicing: What does 'QuizLock'[0:4] evaluate to?
questions.explanation: Slice [0:4] takes characters at indices 0, 1, 2, and 3: 'Q', 'u', 'i', 'z'.
questions.hintText: The end index 4 is exclusive, taking the first 4 letters.

questions.question: Geometry: What is the area of a right-angled triangle with base 6 cm and height 8 cm?
questions.explanation: Area = (base × height) / 2 = (6 × 8) / 2 = 48 / 2 = 24 cm².
questions.hintText: Divide the rectangle area (6 × 8) by 2.

questions.question: Mechanics: A simple lever has an effort arm of 4 meters and a load arm of 1 meter. What is its mechanical advantage?
questions.explanation: Mechanical advantage of a lever = Effort Arm / Load Arm = 4 m / 1 m = 4.
questions.hintText: Divide the effort arm length by the load arm length.

questions.question: LCM: What is the Least Common Multiple (LCM) of 4 and 6?
questions.explanation: Multiples of 4: 4, 8, 12... Multiples of 6: 6, 12... The smallest common multiple is 12.
questions.hintText: Find the smallest number that can be divided by both 4 and 6 without remainder.

questions.question: Atmosphere: Which atmospheric gas is the most abundant by volume in Earth's air (~78%)?
questions.explanation: Nitrogen makes up approximately 78% of Earth's atmosphere, followed by oxygen at ~21%.
questions.hintText: It is NOT oxygen, which is only about 21%.

questions.question: Python Logic: What is the result of expression: `(5 > 3) and (2 > 10)`?
questions.explanation: 5 > 3 is True, but 2 > 10 is False. In boolean AND, True and False produces False.
questions.hintText: Both conditions must be true for AND to evaluate to True.

questions.question: Speed & Time: A cyclist travels 30 km in 40 minutes. What is their average speed in km/h?
questions.explanation: 40 minutes is 2/3 of an hour. Speed = 30 / (2/3) = 30 × 3 / 2 = 45 km/h.
questions.hintText: Convert 40 minutes to hours (2/3 hr), then speed = distance / time.

questions.question: Astronomy: Why does Earth experience four distinct seasons (Spring, Summer, Autumn, Winter)?
questions.optionsString: Earth's distance from the Sun changes dramatically|Earth's rotational axis is tilted by ~23.5 degrees|The Sun burns hotter during July and August|The Moon pulls Earth's climate bands
questions.explanation: Earth's 23.5° axial tilt causes different hemispheres to receive sunlight at different angles as it orbits the Sun.
questions.hintText: It is caused by the tilt of Earth's axis, not distance from the Sun.

questions.question: Angles: In a regular hexagon, what is the measure of each interior angle in degrees?
questions.hintText: Formula: (n - 2) × 180° / n with n = 6.

questions.question: Algorithm Output: What will this loop print: `x = 1; while x < 10: x *= 2; print(x)`?
questions.explanation: x starts at 1, becomes 2, then 4, then 8 (8 < 10 is true), then 16. 16 < 10 is false, so it prints 16.

questions.question: Geometry Volume: A cube has surface area of 150 cm². What is the volume of this cube in cm³?
questions.explanation: A cube has 6 faces: 6a² = 150 => a² = 25 => a = 5 cm. Volume = a³ = 5³ = 125 cm³.
questions.hintText: Find the side length a first: 6 × a² = 150.

questions.question: Optics: When white light passes through a glass triangular prism, which color refracts (bends) the MOST?
questions.explanation: Violet light has the shortest wavelength in the visible spectrum and refracts the most through glass.
questions.hintText: Shortest wavelength bends the most; red has the longest and bends the least.

questions.question: Percentages: A jacket originally priced at $80 is discounted to $64. What is the percentage discount?
questions.hintText: Calculate the difference (16), then divide by the original price (80).

questions.question: Circuits: Three identical 6-Ohm resistors are connected in PARALLEL. What is the equivalent resistance?
questions.explanation: For parallel resistors: 1/R = 1/6 + 1/6 + 1/6 = 3/6 = 1/2 => R = 2 Ω.
questions.hintText: When n identical resistors are in parallel, equivalent R = R_single / n.

questions.question: Data Logic: Which data structure operates on a First-In, First-Out (FIFO) principle like a supermarket checkout line?
questions.explanation: A Queue processes elements FIFO (First In, First Out). A Stack is LIFO.
questions.hintText: Think of people waiting in a queue.

questions.question: Probability: A fair coin is tossed 3 times. What is the total number of possible distinct outcome sequences?
questions.explanation: Each toss has 2 outcomes: 2 × 2 × 2 = 2³ = 8 outcomes (HHH, HHT, HTH, HTT, THH, THT, TTH, TTT).
questions.hintText: Multiply 2 possibilities for each of the 3 tosses: 2³.

questions.question: Astronomy: What is the name of the boundary around a black hole beyond which nothing, not even light, can escape?
questions.explanation: The Event Horizon is the theoretical boundary where the escape velocity exceeds the speed of light.
questions.hintText: It is called the 'horizon' of events.

questions.question: Combinatorics: How many unique ways can 5 friends stand in a single line for a group photo (5!)?
questions.explanation: 5! = 5 × 4 × 3 × 2 × 1 = 120 unique permutations.
questions.hintText: Calculate 5 factorial: 5 × 4 × 3 × 2 × 1.

questions.question: Right Triangle Geometry: If a right triangle has legs a = 5 and b = 12, what is the hypotenuse c?
questions.explanation: By the Pythagorean Theorem: c = √(5² + 12²) = √(25 + 144) = √169 = 13.

questions.question: Syllogism Deduction: All metals conduct electricity. Copper is a metal. What follows logically?
questions.optionsString: Copper conducts electricity|All conductors are copper|Copper is an insulator|Some metals do not conduct
questions.explanation: By universal instantiation (Modus Ponens): if every member of set M has property E, and C ∈ M, then C has property E.
questions.hintText: Apply the rule for all metals to copper.

questions.question: Newton's Second Law: What net force F (in Newtons) is required to accelerate a 5 kg mass at 4 m/s²?
questions.explanation: By Newton's Second Law: F = m × a = 5 kg × 4 m/s² = 20 N.
questions.hintText: Multiply mass m (5 kg) by acceleration a (4 m/s²).

questions.question: SAT Vocabulary: Choose the best synonym for 'PRAGMATIC':
questions.explanation: 'Pragmatic' means dealing with things sensibly and realistically in a practical way.
questions.hintText: A pragmatic engineer focuses on practical real-world results.

questions.question: Binary Arithmetic: What is the decimal (base-10) value of the 4-bit binary number 1010₂?
questions.hintText: Add the place values for 8 and 2 (8 + 2).

questions.question: Logarithm Blitz: What is log₂(256)? (To what power must 2 be raised to equal 256?)
questions.explanation: Since 2⁸ = 256, log₂(256) = 8.

questions.question: Trigonometry: For any angle θ, what is the exact value of sin²(θ) + cos²(θ)?
questions.explanation: The fundamental Pythagorean trigonometric identity states sin²(θ) + cos²(θ) = 1.
questions.hintText: Derived directly from the unit circle where x² + y² = 1.

questions.question: Chemistry & Physics: What is the pH value of pure neutral water at 25 °C?
questions.explanation: Pure water has equal concentrations of H⁺ and OH⁻ ions, yielding a neutral pH of exactly 7.
questions.hintText: The midpoint of the 0 to 14 pH scale.

questions.question: Logarithms: What is the value of log₁₀(1000)?
questions.hintText: Count the zeros: 10 to what power gives 1000?

questions.question: Computer Science: How many bits are in one standard Byte?
questions.explanation: 1 Byte is defined as exactly 8 bits (capable of representing 256 distinct values).
questions.hintText: One byte consists of 8 binary digits.

questions.question: Quadratic Discriminant: For ax² + bx + c = 0, what does a discriminant D = b² - 4ac > 0 indicate about the roots?
questions.optionsString: No real roots (two complex roots)|Two distinct real roots|Exactly one real root (multiplicity 2)|All roots are zero
questions.explanation: When D > 0, the quadratic formula yields two distinct real solutions.
questions.hintText: When D is strictly positive, the square root produces +√D and -√D.

questions.question: Kinetic Energy: What is the kinetic energy (in Joules) of an 8 kg projectile moving at 10 m/s (E = ½mv²)?
questions.hintText: Square 10 first (100), multiply by 8 (800), then take half.

questions.question: Vectors: What is the magnitude (length) of 2D vector v = (3, 4)?
questions.hintText: Use the Pythagorean theorem: √(x² + y²).

questions.question: Waves: A sound wave has a frequency of 170 Hz and travels at 340 m/s in air. What is its wavelength λ?
questions.explanation: λ = v / f = 340 m/s / 170 Hz = 2.0 meters.
questions.hintText: Formula: wavelength = wave speed / frequency (340 / 170).

questions.question: Hexadecimal: What is the decimal value of the hexadecimal number 0x1F?
questions.hintText: In hex, F equals 15 in decimal. 1 × 16 + 15 = ?

questions.question: Algebra: If log₂(x) + log₂(4) = 3, what is x?
questions.hintText: log(a) + log(b) = log(ab), so log₂(4x) = 3.

questions.question: Electromagnetism: Which device transforms electrical energy into mechanical rotational kinetic energy?
questions.explanation: An electric motor converts electrical energy into rotational mechanical motion using Lorentz forces.
questions.hintText: Generators do the opposite; motors create movement from electricity.

questions.question: Combinations: How many combinations of 3 books can be chosen from a shelf of 5 books (C(5, 3))?
questions.hintText: C(5, 3) is the same as C(5, 2) = (5 × 4) / 2.

questions.question: Boolean Logic: According to De Morgan's Law, what is NOT (A AND B) equivalent to?
questions.optionsString: (NOT A) AND (NOT B)|(NOT A) OR (NOT B)|NOT (A OR B)|A OR B
questions.explanation: De Morgan's first law: ¬(A ∧ B) ≡ (¬A) ∨ (¬B).
questions.hintText: Negating an AND flips it to an OR between the negated variables.

questions.question: Thermodynamics: What is absolute zero in degrees Celsius (the temperature at which thermal motion ceases)?
questions.explanation: Absolute zero (0 Kelvin) corresponds to -273.15 °C.
questions.hintText: Zero Kelvin in Celsius scale is approximately -273 °C.

questions.question: Geometric Series: What is the infinite sum S = 2 + 1 + 1/2 + 1/4 + 1/8 + ...?
questions.explanation: Formula S = a / (1 - r) with initial term a = 2 and common ratio r = 1/2: S = 2 / (1 - 0.5) = 4.
questions.hintText: Use S = a / (1 - r) with a = 2 and r = 1/2.

questions.question: Nuclear Physics: If a radioactive isotope has a half-life of 4 hours, what fraction remains after 12 hours?
questions.explanation: 12 hours = 3 half-lives. Remaining fraction = (1/2)³ = 1/8.
questions.hintText: 12 / 4 = 3 half-life cycles: half, quarter, eighth.

questions.question: Geometry: What is the area of a trapezoid with parallel bases 8 cm and 12 cm, and height 6 cm?
questions.hintText: Average of bases ((8 + 12)/2 = 10) multiplied by height 6.

questions.question: Algorithms: What is the average time complexity of searching in a Balanced Binary Search Tree (AVL or Red-Black)?
questions.explanation: Because the height of a balanced tree with n nodes is bounded by log₂(n), search takes O(log n).
questions.hintText: Each step cuts the remaining search space in half.

questions.question: Optics: What optical phenomenon explains why diamonds exhibit such brilliant sparkle and fire?
questions.explanation: Diamonds have a high refractive index (2.42) and small critical angle (~24.4°), trapping light via total internal reflection.
questions.hintText: Light bounces inside the facets because it cannot escape at steep angles.

questions.question: Calculus Intuition: What is the instantaneous rate of change (derivative dy/dx) of y = x² at the point where x = 1?
questions.explanation: The power rule gives dy/dx = 2x. Evaluated at x = 1, the slope is 2(1) = 2.
questions.hintText: The derivative of x² is 2x.

questions.question: Relativity: According to Einstein's mass-energy equivalence equation E = mc², what does 'c' represent?
questions.optionsString: Speed of light in vacuum|Speed of sound|Capacitance|Coulomb's constant
questions.explanation: In E = mc², c is the speed of light in vacuum (~3 × 10⁸ m/s).
questions.hintText: The universal speed limit of our universe.

questions.question: Combinatorics: How many total possible outcomes exist when rolling three standard 6-sided dice simultaneously (6³)?
questions.explanation: Each die has 6 faces: 6 × 6 × 6 = 6³ = 216 distinct outcomes.
questions.hintText: Multiply 6 by itself 3 times: 6 × 6 = 36, then 36 × 6 = ?

questions.question: Bitwise Operations: What is the result of the bitwise XOR operation `5 ^ 3` (in binary: `101₂ ^ 011₂`)?
questions.hintText: XOR outputs 1 when bits differ: (1^0=1), (0^1=1), (1^1=0) -> 110₂ = 6.

questions.question: Fluid Dynamics: According to Bernoulli's principle, when the velocity of a flowing fluid increases, what happens to its static pressure?
questions.optionsString: It decreases|It increases|It remains constant|It becomes negative
questions.explanation: Bernoulli's principle states that an increase in fluid speed occurs simultaneously with a decrease in static pressure.
questions.hintText: Higher speed means lower pressure (the principle that helps generate airplane wing lift).

questions.question: Probability: What is the probability of rolling a sum of 8 with two fair 6-sided dice?
questions.explanation: Pairs summing to 8: (2,6), (3,5), (4,4), (5,3), (6,2) — exactly 5 combinations out of 36.

questions.question: Quantum Physics: What does the Heisenberg Uncertainty Principle state cannot be measured simultaneously with arbitrary precision?
questions.optionsString: Mass and charge|Position and momentum|Temperature and pressure|Velocity and acceleration
questions.explanation: Heisenberg's principle states Δx × Δp ≥ ℏ/2; exact position and momentum cannot both be known simultaneously.
questions.hintText: Where a particle is, and how fast it is moving (position & momentum).

questions.question: Modular Arithmetic: What is 17 mod 5?
questions.explanation: 17 = 3 × 5 + 2, so the remainder (17 mod 5) is 2.
questions.hintText: Subtract the nearest multiple of 5 (15) from 17.

questions.question: Fibonacci Matrix: 1, 1, 2, 3, 5, 8, 13, ... What is the next number in this sequence?
questions.explanation: Each Fibonacci term is the sum of the two preceding terms: F_n = F_(n-1) + F_(n-2) = 8 + 13 = 21.
questions.hintText: Add the last two numbers together: 8 + 13.

questions.question: Cubic Progression: Look at the sequence of cubes: 1, 8, 27, 64, ... What is the 5th term (5³)?
questions.explanation: The sequence is n³: 1³=1, 2³=8, 3³=27, 4³=64, and 5³ = 5 × 5 × 5 = 125.
questions.hintText: Compute 5³ = 5 × 5 × 5.

questions.question: Exponential Growth Riddle: A patch of lily pads doubles in size every day. If it covers the entire lake on Day 30, on which day did it cover HALF the lake?
questions.explanation: Because the patch doubles every single day, one day before reaching 100% (Day 30) it covered 50% — on Day 29!
questions.hintText: Work backwards one day from Day 30!

questions.question: Spatial Clock IQ: Through how many degrees does the minute hand of an analog clock rotate in 2.5 minutes?
questions.explanation: The minute hand completes 360° in 60 minutes (6° per minute). In 2.5 minutes: 2.5 × 6° = 15°.
questions.hintText: 360° / 60 min = 6° per minute. Multiply 6° × 2.5.

questions.question: Three-Box Paradox: Gold is in 1 of 3 boxes. Box A says: 'The gold is in here.' Box B says: 'The gold is not in here.' Box C says: 'The gold is not in Box A.' If ONLY ONE label is true, where is the gold?
questions.explanation: If gold is in Box B: A is false, B is false, and C ('not in A') is true — exactly 1 true statement!
questions.hintText: Test putting the gold in Box B: then both A and B lie, and only C tells the truth!

questions.question: Combinatorics IQ: How many distinct 4-digit PIN codes can be formed using the digits {1, 2, 3, 4} without repeating any digit (4!)?
questions.explanation: 4! = 4 × 3 × 2 × 1 = 24 unique permutations.
questions.hintText: Compute 4 factorial: 4 × 3 × 2 × 1.

questions.question: Prime Detective: What is the only even prime number in mathematics?
questions.explanation: 2 is the only even prime number, because every other even number is divisible by 2.
questions.hintText: The smallest positive prime number.

questions.question: Pattern Matrix: 1, 4, 9, 16, 25, ... What is the 6th term?
questions.explanation: The sequence of perfect squares: n² => 6² = 36.
questions.hintText: Square of 6 (6 × 6).

questions.question: Spatial Reasoning: A standard six-sided die has opposite sides that always sum to what number?
questions.explanation: On any standard gaming die, opposite faces always sum to 7 (1+6, 2+5, 3+4).
questions.hintText: 1 is opposite 6, 2 is opposite 5...

questions.question: Geometry: A standard cube has 6 faces and 8 vertices. How many edges does it have?
questions.explanation: By Euler's polyhedron formula V - E + F = 2: 8 - E + 6 = 2 => E = 12 edges.
questions.hintText: 4 top edges + 4 bottom edges + 4 vertical pillar edges.

questions.question: Pigeonhole Principle: In a dark room with 12 black socks and 12 blue socks, what is the minimum socks you must draw to GUARANTEE a matching pair?
questions.explanation: There are 2 colors (pigeonholes). Drawing 3 socks guarantees at least two of the same color.
questions.hintText: If the first two are different colors, the 3rd must match one of them.

questions.question: Number Matrix: What is the missing number in the sequence: 2, 5, 10, 17, 26, 37, ...?
questions.explanation: Differences are consecutive odd numbers: +3, +5, +7, +9, +11, +13. 37 + 13 = 50 (or n² + 1).
questions.hintText: Each term is n² + 1: 7² + 1 = 49 + 1 = 50.

questions.question: Knights & Knaves: Person A says 'I am a knave (liar)'. Can this person exist on the island?
questions.optionsString: Yes, A is a knave|No, this statement is a logical paradox|Yes, A is a knight|Yes, but only on alternating days
questions.explanation: A knight cannot say it (it would be a lie), and a knave cannot say it (it would be true). It's an impossible paradox.
questions.hintText: If a knight says it, he lies. If a knave says it, he speaks the truth.

questions.question: Alternating Series: 3, 5, 9, 15, 23, 33, ... What comes next?
questions.explanation: Differences are +2, +4, +6, +8, +10. Next difference is +12 => 33 + 12 = 45.
questions.hintText: Differences increase by 2 each step: +2, +4, +6, +8, +10, +12.

questions.question: Cubic Geometry: A 3×3×3 large cube is painted red on the outside and cut into 27 unit cubes. How many unit cubes have RED PAINT ON EXACTLY TWO FACES?
questions.explanation: Cubes with 2 painted faces lie along the edges (excluding corners): 12 edges × 1 = 12 cubes.
questions.hintText: These cubes are along the middle of the 12 edges of the big cube.

questions.question: Cubic Geometry: In the same 3×3×3 painted cube cut into 27 small cubes, how many have RED PAINT ON EXACTLY THREE FACES?
questions.explanation: Only the 8 corner cubes have 3 painted faces.
questions.hintText: How many corners does a cube have?

questions.question: Cognitive Matrix: Look at the triplets: (2, 3, 13), (3, 4, 25), (4, 5, 41). Following the rule a² + b² = c, what is the third value for (5, 6, ?)?
questions.hintText: Sum of squares: 25 + 36.

questions.question: Speed River Riddle: A boat travels 12 km downstream in 1 hour and returns upstream in 2 hours. What is the speed of the river current?
questions.explanation: v_down = 12 km/h, v_up = 6 km/h. Current speed = (v_down - v_up) / 2 = (12 - 6) / 2 = 3 km/h.
questions.hintText: Half the difference between downstream and upstream speeds.

questions.question: Deductive Grid: Three friends (Alice, Bob, Carol) wear red, blue, green hats. Alice is not wearing red. Carol is wearing green. What color is Alice's hat?
questions.explanation: Carol wears green. Red is left for Bob because Alice cannot wear red. Thus Alice wears blue.
questions.hintText: Carol has green. If Alice can't have red, she must have blue.

questions.question: Mersenne Primes: A Mersenne number has form 2^p - 1. Which of the following is a Mersenne prime?
questions.explanation: 2⁷ - 1 = 128 - 1 = 127 is a prime number. 15=3×5, 63=7×9, 511=7×73 are composite.

questions.question: Two Child Paradox: A family has two children. You are told that AT LEAST ONE is a boy. What is the probability that BOTH are boys?
questions.explanation: Possible gender pairs: {BB, BG, GB, GG}. Knowing at least one is a boy eliminates GG, leaving {BB, BG, GB}. Only BB has both boys: 1/3.
questions.hintText: Sample space reduces from 4 to 3 outcomes (BB, BG, GB).

questions.question: Angle on Clock: What is the angle between the hour hand and minute hand of a clock at exactly 3:15?
questions.explanation: At 3:15, the minute hand is at 90°. The hour hand has moved 15 min × 0.5°/min = 7.5° past 90°. The angle is 7.5°.
questions.hintText: The hour hand moves 0.5° each minute, so it is not pointing directly at 3!

questions.question: Binary Balance Riddle: What is the maximum number of coins from which you can detect 1 counterfeit heavier coin using 4 weighings on balance scales (3⁴)?
questions.explanation: Each balance scale comparison yields 3 outcomes (left heavier, equal, right heavier). 3⁴ = 81 coins.
questions.hintText: Ternary powers: 3^k where k is the number of weighings.

questions.question: Cognitive Matrix: If all Zorks are Flips, and no Flips are Glims, which conclusion MUST be true?
questions.optionsString: Some Glims are Zorks|All Glims are Flips|No Zorks are Glims|All Zorks are Glims
questions.explanation: Since the set of Zorks is entirely inside Flips, and Flips has zero intersection with Glims, Zorks has zero intersection with Glims.
questions.hintText: Zork is inside Flip; Flip is outside Glim.

questions.question: Polyhedral Duality: An octahedron has 8 triangular faces and 6 vertices. What is its dual Platonic solid?
questions.explanation: The dual swaps faces and vertices: 8 vertices and 6 faces corresponds to the Cube.
questions.hintText: Faces become vertices and vertices become faces: 6 vertices -> 6 faces.

questions.question: Logic Deduction: If statement 'A implies B' is TRUE, what other statement is GUARANTEED to be true?
questions.optionsString: NOT B implies NOT A (Contrapositive)|B implies A (Converse)|NOT A implies NOT B (Inverse)|A AND B are both true
questions.explanation: The contrapositive (¬B → ¬A) is logically equivalent to the original conditional (A → B).
questions.hintText: If P implies Q, then not Q implies not P.

questions.question: Sudoku Logic: In a standard 9×9 Sudoku grid, what is the sum of numbers 1 through 9 in ANY completed row, column, or 3×3 box?
questions.explanation: The sum of integers 1 to 9 is n(n+1)/2 = 9 × 10 / 2 = 45.

questions.question: Paradoxes: A barber in a town shaves only those men who DO NOT shave themselves. Does the barber shave himself?
questions.optionsString: Yes, he definitely does|It is Russell's Paradox (neither answer is consistent)|No, his apprentice shaves him|He must have a full beard
questions.explanation: Russell's Paradox: If he shaves himself, he breaks the rule. If he doesn't shave himself, he must shave himself.
questions.hintText: If he does, he shouldn't. If he doesn't, he must.

questions.question: Prisoners & Hats: 3 prisoners are in a line looking forward: C sees B and A; B sees A; A sees nobody. Hats are from {2 black, 3 white}. All see black on A and white on B. Can C deduce their hat color?
questions.optionsString: No, C has no information|Yes, C has a black hat|Yes, C has a white hat|Only if B speaks first
questions.explanation: If C had black, B would see two black hats (A and C) and know his own is white. Since C sees A black and B white, knowing B is silent allows C to deduce his hat is white.
questions.hintText: Think about what B would conclude if C had a black hat.

questions.question: Combinatorics: What is the number of derangements of 3 items (permutations where NO element appears in its original position)?
questions.hintText: For (A, B, C), the only complete derangements are (B, C, A) and (C, A, B).

questions.question: Cognitive Matrix: Look at: 2 -> 6, 3 -> 12, 4 -> 20, 5 -> 30. What does 7 map to under the rule n(n + 1)?
questions.hintText: Multiply 7 by 8.

questions.question: Set Theory: How many distinct subsets does a finite set of 7 elements contain (including empty set and itself)?
questions.explanation: The power set of a set with n elements has 2^n subsets: 2⁷ = 128.
questions.hintText: 2 to the 7th power (2⁷).

questions.question: God's Number in Rubik's Cube: What is the maximum number of moves required to solve ANY scrambled 3×3×3 Rubik's Cube in half-turn metric?
questions.explanation: Proven mathematically in 2010 using supercomputers, 'God's Number' for the 3×3×3 cube is exactly 20 moves.
questions.hintText: It was proven to be exactly twenty moves.

questions.question: Spider-Legs Math! One spider has 8 legs. How many legs do 7 spiders have altogether? (7 × 8)
questions.explanation: 7 groups of 8 equals 56 (7 × 8 = 56). Fun memory trick: 5, 6, 7, 8 → 56 = 7 × 8!
questions.hintText: Count 7 × 8: remember the sequence 5, 6, 7, 8 → 56 = 7 × 8!

questions.question: A square garden has 4 equal sides. Each side is 6 meters long. What is the perimeter (total distance around) in meters?
questions.explanation: The perimeter of a square is P = 4 × a. With side a = 6 m, P = 4 × 6 = 24 meters.
questions.hintText: Add all 4 equal sides together: 6 + 6 + 6 + 6 (or 4 × 6).

questions.question: Time Explorer: How many minutes are there in 1 and a half hours (1.5 hours)?
questions.explanation: 1 hour (60 min) + half an hour (30 min) = 60 + 30 = 90 minutes.
questions.hintText: 1 hour = 60 minutes, and half an hour = 30 minutes. Add 60 + 30.

questions.question: Piggy Bank Change: You have a 100-cent (1 Dollar) coin and buy a sticker pack for 65 cents. How many cents change do you get back?
questions.explanation: 100 − 65 = 35 cents change (because 65 + 35 = 100).
questions.hintText: Subtract 65 from 100: 100 − 60 = 40, and 40 − 5 = ?

questions.question: Farmyard Riddle: Mia sees 3 ducks and 2 cows in a meadow. Each duck has 2 legs and each cow has 4 legs. How many legs are there in total?
questions.explanation: 3 ducks × 2 legs = 6 legs. 2 cows × 4 legs = 8 legs. Total: 6 + 8 = 14 legs!
questions.hintText: 3 ducks have 6 legs, and 2 cows have 8 legs. Add 6 + 8!

questions.question: Sister Age Riddle: When Leo was 6 years old, his little sister Anna was half his age (3). Now Leo is 10 years old. How old is Anna now?
questions.optionsString: 5 years old|7 years old|8 years old|6 years old
questions.explanation: Anna is 3 years younger than Leo (6 − 3 = 3). When Leo is 10, Anna is 10 − 3 = 7 years old!
questions.hintText: The age difference between Leo and Anna always stays 3 years (10 − 3).

questions.question: Multiplication Table: What is 6 × 4?
questions.explanation: 6 groups of 4 equals 24 (6 × 4 = 24).
questions.hintText: Add 6 four times: 6 + 6 = 12, 12 + 12 = 24.

questions.question: Clock Explorer: How many hours are there in one complete day and night?
questions.explanation: One full Earth day has 24 hours.
questions.hintText: Two 12-hour clock rotations = 24 hours.

questions.question: Geometry Shapes: How many sides does a pentagon have?
questions.explanation: A pentagon is a polygon with exactly 5 sides and 5 angles.
questions.hintText: Penta means five in Greek.

questions.question: Multiplication Fun: What is 9 × 5?
questions.hintText: Count by fives nine times: 5, 10, 15, ..., 45.

questions.question: Money Math: If you have two 25-cent coins (quarters), how many cents do you have in total?
questions.explanation: 25¢ + 25¢ = 50¢ (half a dollar).
questions.hintText: 25 plus 25 equals 50.

questions.question: Addition Trail: 5 + 5 + 5 = ?
questions.explanation: Three 5s equal 3 × 5 = 15.
questions.hintText: 5 + 5 = 10, then add 5 more.

questions.question: Calendar Fun: How many days are in one week?
questions.explanation: A week consists of 7 days: Monday through Sunday.
questions.hintText: Count Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday, Thursday, Friday, Saturday, Sunday.

questions.question: Even Numbers: Which of these numbers is an EVEN number (ends in 0, 2, 4, 6, 8)?
questions.explanation: 30 ends in 0, so it is divisible by 2 and even.
questions.hintText: Even numbers can be split into two equal whole halves.

questions.question: Multiplication Table: What is 4 × 9?
questions.hintText: Double 9 twice: 9 -> 18 -> 36.

questions.question: Riddle on the Lake: There are 8 ducks swimming. 7 more fly in to join them. How many ducks are there now?
questions.explanation: 8 + 7 = 15 ducks.

questions.question: Perimeter: A rectangle is 5 cm long and 3 cm wide. What is its perimeter?
questions.explanation: Perimeter = 2 × (length + width) = 2 × (5 + 3) = 2 × 8 = 16 cm.
questions.hintText: Add all 4 sides: 5 + 3 + 5 + 3 = 16.

questions.question: Multiplication Table: What is 7 × 6?
questions.hintText: 7 × 5 = 35, plus 7 more equals 42.

questions.question: Counting By Fives: 5, 10, 15, 20, ... What is the missing number?
questions.explanation: Adding 5 each step: 20 + 5 = 25.
questions.hintText: Add 5 to 20.

questions.question: Fair Sharing: You have 18 candies to share equally among 3 friends. How many candies does each friend get?
questions.explanation: 18 divided by 3 is 6 (18 ÷ 3 = 6).

questions.question: Egg Cartons: One full carton holds 12 eggs (one dozen). How many eggs are in 2 cartons?
questions.hintText: Double 12: 12 + 12.

questions.question: Multiplication Table: What is 9 × 7?
Subtraction Riddle: Max had 45 toy bricks. He used 25 of them to build a tower. How many bricks does he have left?
questions.explanation: 45 - 25 = 20 bricks.

questions.question: Fractions: What is half of 1/2 of an apple?
questions.explanation: Half of a half is 1/4 (one quarter).
questions.hintText: If you cut a half into two equal pieces, each is 1/4.

questions.question: Multiplication Table: What is 8 × 9?
Time Mystery: A movie starts at 4:15 PM and ends at 4:50 PM. How many minutes long was the movie?
questions.explanation: 50 - 15 = 35 minutes.
questions.hintText: Subtract 15 from 50.

questions.question: Squares: What is 8 × 8?
questions.hintText: Chessboard has 8 rows of 8 squares = 64 squares.

questions.question: Perimeter: An equilateral triangle has three equal sides of 9 cm each. What is its perimeter?
questions.hintText: Add 9 three times: 9 + 9 + 9.

questions.question: Balance Riddle: A toy robot weighs as much as 2 toy cars. If 1 toy car weighs 3 kg, how much does the robot weigh?
questions.explanation: 2 × 3 kg = 6 kg.
questions.hintText: Multiply 2 by 3.

questions.question: Place Value: In the number 472, what is the value of the digit 4?
questions.explanation: The digit 4 is in the hundreds place, representing 400.
questions.hintText: 4 hundreds, 7 tens, and 2 ones.

questions.question: Age Logic: Two years ago, Emma was 8 years old. How old will she be 4 years from NOW?
questions.explanation: Two years ago she was 8, so now she is 8 + 2 = 10. In 4 years: 10 + 4 = 14.
questions.hintText: Find her age today first: 8 + 2 = 10.

questions.question: Division with Remainder: If you divide 17 marbles equally among 4 bags, how many marbles are left over?
questions.explanation: 17 = (4 × 4) + 1. Each bag gets 4 marbles, and 1 marble is left over.
questions.hintText: 4 × 4 = 16. How many to reach 17?

questions.question: Centimeter & Meter: How many centimeters (cm) are in 1 meter?
questions.explanation: 1 meter = 100 centimeters.
questions.hintText: The prefix 'centi-' means one hundredth.

packs.title: Junior Scientists (7–9 yrs): Nature, Space & Matter

questions.question: When liquid water (H₂O) cools down to 0 °C (32 °F), it freezes into a solid. What do we call solid water?
questions.explanation: At 0 °C, liquid water (H₂O) freezes into solid ice crystals!
questions.hintText: Think of what you put in a cold drink or skate on in winter!

questions.question: Magnet Magic: Every magnet has a North (N) pole and a South (S) pole. What happens when you bring a North pole close to a South pole?
questions.optionsString: They pull together (attract)|They push apart (repel)|They melt|They turn into glass
questions.explanation: Opposite magnetic poles (North and South) attract each other, while same poles (N–N or S–S) push apart!
questions.hintText: Opposite poles (N and S) like each other and pull together!

questions.question: Solar System Explorer: Which planet is the 3rd planet from the Sun and our home with liquid oceans of H₂O?
questions.explanation: Order from the Sun: 1. Mercury, 2. Venus, 3. Earth, 4. Mars. Earth is the 3rd planet!
questions.hintText: Count outward from the Sun: 1. Mercury, 2. Venus, 3. ...?

questions.question: Green Leaves Factory: Plants use sunlight, water (H₂O), and carbon dioxide (CO₂) to make food and release which gas that we breathe?
questions.explanation: During photosynthesis, green plants take in CO₂ and H₂O and release fresh oxygen (O₂) into the air!
questions.hintText: It is the gas in the air that humans and animals need to breathe (O₂).

questions.question: Rainbow Science: What happens when white sunlight shines through tiny raindrops in the sky?
questions.optionsString: It splits into 7 rainbow colors|It turns pitch black|It freezes into hail|It makes thunder
questions.explanation: Raindrops act like tiny glass prisms, bending white sunlight into the 7 colors of the rainbow!
questions.hintText: Sunlight is actually made of all the colors of the rainbow mixed together!

questions.question: How many major planets orbit the Sun in our Solar System (from Mercury out to Neptune)?
questions.explanation: There are 8 major planets: Mercury, Venus, Earth, Mars, Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus, and Neptune.
questions.hintText: 4 rocky inner planets + 4 giant outer planets = 8 planets.

questions.question: Human Body: Which organ in your chest pumps blood through your entire body all day and night?
questions.explanation: The heart pumps oxygen-rich blood through your arteries and veins.
questions.hintText: It beats steadily: thump-thump, thump-thump.

questions.question: Plant Life: Which part of a plant grows downward into the soil to absorb water and minerals?
questions.explanation: Roots anchor the plant in soil and absorb water and nutrients.
questions.hintText: They grow underground.

questions.question: The 5 Senses: Which sense organ allows you to hear music and sounds?
questions.explanation: Ears capture sound vibrations in the air and send signals to your brain.
questions.hintText: You use them to listen.

questions.question: Animal World: Which of these animals is NOCTURNAL (active mainly at night)?
questions.explanation: Owls hunt at night and sleep during the day, making them nocturnal.
questions.hintText: It has big eyes and hoots in the dark.

questions.question: Earth Science: What falls from clouds as precipitation during cold winter when water freezes?
questions.explanation: When water vapor freezes into ice crystals in cold air, it falls as snow.
questions.hintText: White flakes you use to build a snowman.

questions.question: Gravity: What happens when you drop an apple from your hand?
questions.optionsString: It floats upward|It falls down toward Earth|It turns sideways|It disappears
questions.explanation: Earth's gravitational force pulls all objects down toward the ground.
questions.hintText: Gravity pulls everything down.

questions.question: Water Cycle: What is the process called when liquid puddle water heats up in the sun and turns into invisible vapor in the air?
questions.explanation: Evaporation is the transition of liquid water into invisible gas (water vapor).
questions.hintText: Sunlight evaporates puddles.

questions.question: Space Science: How long does it take for Earth to complete ONE full orbit around the Sun?
questions.explanation: Earth takes about 365.25 days (one full year) to orbit the Sun once.
questions.hintText: 365 days = 1 year.

questions.question: Animal Classification: Animals with backbones (spines) are called vertebrates. Which of these is an INVERTEBRATE (no bones)?
questions.explanation: Jellyfish have soft bodies with no skeleton or backbone (invertebrates).
questions.hintText: It has no bones at all and floats in the ocean.

questions.question: Light & Shadows: Why do objects cast shadows on the ground on a sunny day?
questions.optionsString: Because light travels in straight lines and the object blocks it|Because the ground absorbs all sunlight|Because the object radiates cold darkness|Because the air gets tired
questions.explanation: Light rays travel in straight lines. When an opaque object blocks the rays, an unlit shadow forms behind it.
questions.hintText: Light cannot bend around the object, so a dark shape forms behind it.

questions.question: Solar System: Which planet is nicknamed the 'Red Planet' because of its rusty iron-rich soil?
questions.explanation: Mars has abundant iron oxide (rust) on its surface, giving it a distinct reddish appearance.
questions.hintText: The 4th planet from the Sun.

questions.question: Ecosystem Food Chains: What do we call animals that eat ONLY plants (like rabbits and cows)?
questions.explanation: Herbivores (from Latin herba = plant) feed exclusively on plant matter.
questions.hintText: Herbs = plants, so herbivores eat plants.

questions.question: Space Science: Why does the Moon appear to change shape (phases: crescent, half, full) from Earth?
questions.optionsString: The Moon physically grows and shrinks|We see different portions of the sunlit side as the Moon orbits Earth|Earth's clouds cover parts of the Moon|The Sun turns off one side of the Moon
questions.explanation: As the Moon circles Earth, our viewpoint of the half illuminated by the Sun changes continually.
questions.hintText: Half of the Moon is always lit by the Sun; we just see it from changing angles.

questions.question: Animal Adaptations: What do we call it when an animal blends into its surroundings (like a chameleon or arctic fox)?
questions.explanation: Camouflage allows animals to disguise their appearance to hide from predators or prey.
questions.hintText: Blends in with colors of trees, snow or rocks.

questions.question: Electricity & Safety: Which of these materials is an ELECTRICAL CONDUCTOR (allows electricity to flow through it)?
questions.explanation: Metals like copper have free electrons and are excellent electrical conductors.
questions.hintText: Electric wires inside cables are made from this shiny metal.

questions.question: Earth Science: What are fossils?
questions.optionsString: Rare rocks formed in space|Preserved remains or impressions of ancient organisms in rock|Pieces of fallen meteorites|Frozen water underground
questions.explanation: Fossils are the mineralized remains of ancient plants, animals, or dinosaur bones preserved in stone.
questions.hintText: How scientists study dinosaurs that lived millions of years ago.

questions.question: Habitats: Which biome has very little rainfall, extreme hot daytime temperatures, and cactus plants?
questions.explanation: Deserts receive less than 25 cm of precipitation annually and support specialized flora like cacti.
questions.hintText: Full of sand dunes and very dry.

questions.question: Sound Science: How is sound created?
questions.optionsString: By light shining brightly|By freezing cold air|By vibrations of matter traveling through a medium|By magnetic fields
questions.explanation: Sound is produced when a vibrating object causes pressure waves in the surrounding air, liquid, or solid.
questions.hintText: Touch your throat while talking: you can feel vibrations!

questions.question: Atmosphere: Which invisible force pulls rain, rivers, and all objects down to the ground?
questions.explanation: Gravity is the attractive force that Earth exerts on all masses.
questions.hintText: The gravitational pull of Earth.

questions.question: Human Skeleton: How many bones does an adult human body have?
questions.explanation: An adult human skeleton consists of 206 distinct bones.
questions.hintText: A little over two hundred bones.

questions.question: Plant Science: What is the green pigment in plant leaves that absorbs sunlight for photosynthesis?
questions.explanation: Chlorophyll absorbs red and blue light from the Sun and gives leaves their green color.
questions.hintText: Starts with 'Chloro-'.

questions.question: Solar System: Which planet is famous for its massive, beautiful system of rings made of ice and rock particles?
questions.explanation: Saturn is the gas giant renowned for its spectacular, wide ring system.
questions.hintText: The 6th planet from the Sun with prominent rings.

questions.question: Weather & Clouds: What causes thunder during a thunderstorm?
questions.optionsString: Clouds crashing together like rocks|Lightning superheating the air rapidly, causing explosive shockwave expansion|Rain falling too fast|Wind shaking the mountains
questions.explanation: Lightning heats the surrounding air channel to ~30,000 °C in milliseconds; the rapid explosive expansion creates thunder.
questions.hintText: Lightning heats the air so fast that it creates an explosive sonic boom.

questions.question: Animal Senses: How do bats navigate and find tiny insects in pitch darkness?
questions.optionsString: Echolocation (emitting ultrasonic clicks and listening to echoes)|Night vision heat goggles|Smelling insects from miles away|Following magnetic compass needles
questions.explanation: Bats use echolocation: high-frequency ultrasound calls bounce off targets and reveal their exact location.
questions.hintText: They use sound echoes to 'see' in the dark.

questions.question: Geology: What is molten liquid rock called while it is STILL underground inside a volcano?
questions.explanation: Underground it is called magma; once it erupts onto the surface it is called lava.
questions.hintText: Magma underground, Lava above ground.

questions.question: Ocean Science: What covers approximately 71% of the entire surface of planet Earth?
questions.explanation: Oceans cover roughly 71% of Earth's surface, which is why Earth is called the 'Blue Marble'.
questions.hintText: Earth is the blue water planet.

questions.question: Chemistry & Air: What gas do humans and animals exhale into the air that green plants absorb?
questions.explanation: Animals breathe in O₂ and exhale CO₂; plants use CO₂ in photosynthesis to generate oxygen.
questions.hintText: CO₂ (carbon dioxide).

questions.question: Junior Chess (White to move): The Black King on g8 is trapped behind its own pawns! Find Checkmate in 1 move!
questions.explanation: 1. Ra8# is the classic Back-Rank Mate! Black's own pawns on f7, g7, and h7 block the King from escaping.
questions.hintText: Slide your White Rook straight up from a1 to the top corner a8!

questions.question: Junior Chess (White to move): Use your Queen and King to deliver Checkmate in 1 move!
questions.explanation: 1. Qf7# is the Queen Support Mate! The White King on f6 protects the Queen on f7 so the Black King on f8 cannot capture her.
questions.hintText: Move your White Queen from f3 straight up to f7 right in front of the Black King!

questions.question: Word Explorer: Which word is the OPPOSITE (antonym) of 'ANCIENT' (very, very old)?
questions.explanation: 'Ancient' means from a very long time ago, so its opposite (antonym) is 'Modern' (new, from today).
questions.hintText: Ancient pyramids are old; today's cities are...

questions.question: Word Explorer: If a turtle walks at a 'SLUGGISH' pace, how is the turtle moving?
questions.optionsString: Very slowly|Super fast|Backwards|High in the sky
questions.explanation: 'Sluggish' (like a garden slug!) means moving very slowly and with low energy.
questions.hintText: Think of how fast a little slug or snail moves!

questions.question: Robot Loop: You program a toy robot with the block: [REPEAT 4 TIMES: Jump 3 steps forward]. How many steps does the robot jump in total?
questions.explanation: A repeat loop runs the instruction 4 times: 3 + 3 + 3 + 3 = 4 × 3 = 12 steps forward!
questions.hintText: Multiply 4 repeats × 3 steps each (3 + 3 + 3 + 3).

questions.question: Robot Compass: Your robot faces NORTH. You run: [Turn Right 90°] then [Turn Right 90°] again. Which direction is the robot facing now?
questions.explanation: Facing North → Turn Right once faces East (90°) → Turn Right a second time faces South (180° opposite)!
questions.hintText: Two right turns (90° + 90° = 180°) make the robot face the opposite way of North!

questions.question: Chess Pieces Value: In standard chess valuation, how many points is a Rook worth?
questions.explanation: Pawn = 1, Knight/Bishop = 3, Rook = 5, Queen = 9.
questions.hintText: Stronger than a Bishop (3) but less than a Queen (9).

questions.question: Word Heroes Synonyms: Which word means the same as 'GIGANTIC'?
questions.explanation: 'Gigantic' and 'Enormous' both describe something exceptionally huge.
questions.hintText: Huge like a giant.

questions.question: Robot Commands: Your robot is at square (0, 0). It executes [MOVE FORWARD 2], then [MOVE FORWARD 3]. How many squares did it move?
questions.explanation: 2 + 3 = 5 squares total.
questions.hintText: 2 plus 3.

questions.question: Chess Movement: Which piece moves in an 'L-shape' (two squares one way, then one square perpendicular) and can jump over other pieces?
questions.explanation: The Knight moves in an L-shape and is the only piece that can jump over others.
questions.hintText: Shaped like a horse.

questions.question: Opposite Antonyms: What is the direct antonym (opposite) of 'BRAVE'?
questions.explanation: The opposite of brave is cowardly (fearful).
questions.hintText: A hero is brave; someone who runs away in fear is...

questions.question: Conditional Logic: In code, if a statement says `IF is_raining == True: take_umbrella() ELSE: wear_sunglasses()`. If it is SUNNY outside, what do you do?
questions.explanation: Since is_raining is False, the code enters the ELSE block: wear_sunglasses().
questions.hintText: If it is sunny, it is NOT raining (ELSE branch).

questions.question: Chess Tactics: What do we call a double attack when one piece attacks TWO enemy pieces simultaneously?
questions.explanation: A fork is a tactical maneuver where a single piece (often a Knight) attacks two enemy pieces at once.
questions.hintText: Like a dining fork with two or more prongs.

questions.question: Compound Words: Which of these words is made of TWO words joined together?
questions.explanation: Butterfly is formed from 'butter' and 'fly'.
questions.hintText: Butter + fly.

questions.question: Repeat Loops: A drawing program repeats: [DRAW LINE, TURN 45°] 8 times. What shape does it draw?
questions.explanation: 8 sides × 45° = 360°, forming a complete 8-sided regular Octagon.
questions.hintText: 8 repetitions create an 8-sided shape.

questions.question: Chess Board: How many total squares are on a standard 8×8 chessboard?
questions.explanation: 8 rows × 8 columns = 64 squares (32 light and 32 dark).
questions.hintText: 8 times 8.

questions.question: Word Master: What is an antonym for 'FREEZE'?
questions.explanation: The opposite of freeze is melt.
questions.hintText: Ice freezes; when it gets warm, it...

questions.question: Variables: You store `apples = 5`. Then you execute `apples = apples + 3`. What is the value stored in apples now?
questions.hintText: Take the old value (5) and add 3.

questions.question: Chess Tactics: What is a 'PIN' in chess?
questions.optionsString: An attack where a piece cannot move without exposing a more valuable piece behind it|When two pawns collide head on|Promoting a pawn to a Queen|Moving two knights simultaneously
questions.explanation: A pin prevents an enemy piece from moving because doing so would expose the King or Queen behind it.
questions.hintText: The pinned piece is 'glued' to its spot to protect what's behind.

questions.question: Word Meanings: What does 'SWIFT' mean?
questions.optionsString: Very heavy|Extremely loud|Very fast and quick|Deep underground
questions.explanation: 'Swift' means moving or capable of moving with great speed.
questions.hintText: The swift bird flies fast.

questions.question: Bug Hunting: A bug in computer programming is:
questions.optionsString: An error or mistake in the code that causes unexpected behavior|A real beetle inside the keyboard|A special feature that speeds up games|A new computer mouse
questions.explanation: A bug is an unintentional coding flaw or logic error in software.
questions.hintText: When code behaves wrongly, programmers 'debug' it.

questions.question: Chess Rules: Can a King EVER move to a square attacked by an enemy piece?
questions.optionsString: Yes, if no other moves exist|No, never (it is an illegal move into check)|Yes, on the first move of the game|Only if capturing a Queen
questions.explanation: Moving the King into check is strictly illegal in chess.
questions.hintText: A King is never allowed to walk into danger.

questions.question: Word Roots: The prefix 'TELE-' (in telephone, telescope, television) comes from Greek and means:
questions.explanation: Greek 'tele' means far or distant (seeing far, hearing far).
questions.hintText: Telescopes look far into space.

questions.question: Algorithm Order: To make a sandwich, which step MUST come first?
questions.optionsString: Eat the sandwich|Take two slices of bread|Put the plate in the dishwasher|Wrap the sandwich in foil
questions.explanation: Algorithms require strict logical order: you must get the bread before making the sandwich.
questions.hintText: You cannot eat or wrap a sandwich before getting bread!

questions.question: Chess Rules: What special pawn capture can ONLY happen immediately after an enemy pawn moves two squares forward from its starting rank?
questions.explanation: En Passant allows a pawn to capture an adjacent enemy pawn that just moved two squares past it.
questions.hintText: French term for 'in passing'.

questions.question: Metaphor vs Simile: A comparison that uses the words 'like' or 'as' (e.g. 'brave as a lion') is called a:
questions.explanation: A simile compares two things using 'like' or 'as'.
questions.hintText: Compares using 'as' or 'like'.

questions.question: Loop Counter: `count = 0; REPEAT 4 TIMES: count = count + 2`. What is count at the end?
questions.explanation: 4 repetitions × 2 = 8.
questions.hintText: Add 2 four times: 2 + 2 + 2 + 2.

questions.question: Chess Tactics: A 'SKEWER' is like a reverse pin: which piece is attacked in FRONT?
questions.optionsString: A pawn is in front and Queen behind|A less valuable piece is in front|A MORE valuable piece is in front and must move, exposing the piece behind|Both pieces have equal value
questions.explanation: In a skewer, the more valuable piece (e.g. King or Queen) is in front and is forced to move, exposing a piece behind.
questions.hintText: The big piece in front has to run, losing the piece behind.

questions.question: Idioms: What does the popular idiom 'A piece of cake' mean?
questions.optionsString: A delicious bakery dessert|Something very easy and simple to do|A very difficult homework assignment|An expensive present
questions.explanation: 'A piece of cake' is an English idiom meaning an effortless, very easy task.
questions.hintText: If a quiz is very easy, it's a piece of cake!

questions.question: Maze Navigation: A robot starts facing East. What commands turn it to face North?
questions.optionsString: Turn Left 90°|Turn Right 90°|Turn Around 180°|Move Forward 1 step
questions.explanation: Facing East (right), turning counter-clockwise (Left 90°) points directly to North (up).
questions.hintText: From East, turn counter-clockwise.

questions.question: Chess Endgames: What is STALEMATE (Пат)?
questions.optionsString: When the King is in check and has no moves (Loss)|When a player has no legal moves and is NOT in check (Draw)|When pawns promote to knights|When clocks run out
questions.explanation: Stalemate occurs when the player to move has no legal moves and their King is NOT in check; the game ends in an immediate DRAW.
questions.hintText: No check, but no legal moves = Draw!

questions.question: Word Families: Which word is an ADJECTIVE (describes a noun)?
questions.explanation: 'Playful' is an adjective (e.g. a playful puppy). 'Play' is a verb, 'Quickly' an adverb, 'Player' a noun.
questions.hintText: Describes how something looks or feels (like a puppy).

questions.question: Binary Digits: Computers store all photos, sounds, and games using binary digits (bits). What TWO numbers make up binary?
questions.explanation: Binary code is base-2, using only the digits 0 and 1 (off and on).
questions.hintText: Zero and one.

packs.subtitle: Interactive 2D FEN mating nets, forks, pins & sacrifices

questions.question: White to move: Deliver Opera Box Mate in 1 with the Rook on d1 supported by the Bishop on g5!
questions.explanation: Paul Morphy's Opera Game motif: 1. Rd8# mates the Black King because the g5 Bishop protects d8!
questions.hintText: The Bishop on g5 covers the d8 square. Slide your Rook from d1 to d8!

questions.question: White to move: Execute Boden's Criss-Cross Bishop Checkmate on c6!
questions.explanation: 1. Ba6# slices across a6-c8 while the f4 Bishop covers d6 and c7!
questions.hintText: Develop the Bishop from f1 to a6 to deliver checkmate on the c8 King.

questions.question: White to move: Epaulette Mate! Black's King on e8 is flanked by its own two Rooks on d8 and f8. Deliver mate with the Queen!
questions.explanation: 1. Qe6# is Epaulette Mate! Black's own rooks on d8 and f8 act like shoulder pads blocking escape.
questions.hintText: Move your Queen from g6 directly in front of the King on e6.

questions.question: White to move: Anastasia's Mate! Knight on e7 controls g8 and g6; slide the Rook to the h-file for mate!
questions.explanation: 1. Rh7# completes Anastasia's Mate—the Knight on e7 takes away g8 and g6 while Black's g7 pawn blocks the King.
questions.hintText: Swing the Rook from d3 to h3 to deliver mate along the h-file!

questions.question: Smothered Mate: What piece delivers the final checkmate in a classic Smothered Mate while the enemy King is surrounded by its own pieces?
questions.explanation: A Knight jumps over pieces to deliver checkmate to a trapped King boxed in by its own army.
questions.hintText: Only the jumping Knight can strike a King hemmed in by its own pawns.

questions.question: Endgame Principles: In a King and Pawn endgame, what critical concept involves placing your King directly opposite the enemy King with one square between them?
questions.explanation: The Opposition is a fundamental weapon to outflank the enemy King and escort your pawn to promotion.
questions.hintText: Direct, distant, or diagonal confrontation between kings.

questions.question: Lucena Position: In the famous Lucena Rook endgame, what is the key tactical technique used to shield the King from vertical checks?
questions.optionsString: Underpromotion to Knight|Perpetual check|Building a bridge with the Rook (on the 4th rank)|Stalemate trick
questions.explanation: The 'Bridge Building' technique uses the Rook on the 4th rank (e.g. Rd4) to block checks and allow the pawn to promote.
questions.hintText: Building a bridge with the rook.

questions.question: Philidor Defense: How does the defending player draw a Rook and Pawn endgame in Philidor's 3rd-rank defense?
questions.optionsString: Keep the Rook on the 6th/3rd rank until the pawn advances, then check relentlessly from behind|Sacrifice the Rook immediately|Attack the enemy King from the side|Trade rooks immediately
questions.explanation: The defending Rook holds the 6th (or 3rd) rank cutting off the King. When the pawn pushes, the Rook checks from behind.
questions.hintText: Guard the rank to stop the King, then drop to the rear for checks.

questions.question: Tactical Motif: What famous sacrifice involves offering a Bishop on h7 (or h2) with check to strip the castled King's shelter?
questions.optionsString: Damiano's Mate|Greek Gift Sacrifice (Bxh7+)|Blackburne's Mate|Legal's Mate
questions.explanation: The Greek Gift (Bxh7+) tears open the King's defense, followed by Ng5+ and Qh5.
questions.hintText: Named after the historic Trojan Horse / Greek gift.

questions.question: Zugzwang: What does the German chess term 'Zugzwang' mean?
questions.optionsString: A rapid counter-attack|A perpetual sequence of checks|Compulsion to move, where any legal move worsens the player's position|A sudden discovered checkmate
questions.explanation: Zugzwang is a situation where obligation to make a move leads to disadvantage or defeat.
questions.hintText: Any move you make makes your position worse.

questions.question: Endgame Geometry: The 'Rule of the Square' allows a player to instantly determine what without calculation?
questions.optionsString: Whether castling is legally permitted|Whether a defending King can catch a passed pawn before it promotes|If a bishop can control two diagonals|How many rooks are active
questions.explanation: If the defending King can step inside the square of the passed pawn, it can catch and stop the pawn.
questions.hintText: Square drawn from the pawn to its promotion square.

questions.question: Pawn Breakthrough: In a 3 vs 3 pawn race on adjacent files (e.g. a7-b7-c7 vs a6-b6-c6), which pawn advance initiates the decisive breakthrough?
questions.optionsString: A flank pawn advance|Pushing the central pawn (e.g. b6) to create open passed paths|Retreating the king|Moving the a-pawn
questions.explanation: Pushing the middle pawn sacrifices it to force a capture, enabling an immediate push of the other pawns to queen.
questions.hintText: Thrust the central pawn forward into the enemy line.

questions.question: Bishop Endgames: When is an endgame with opposite-colored bishops notoriously prone to end in a draw?
questions.optionsString: Even when one side is down one or two pawns, because the defender establishes an impenetrable blockade on their color|Only when all pawns are traded|Never, opposite bishops always produce decisive wins|Only on move 50
questions.explanation: Opposite-colored bishops cannot challenge each other, enabling the defender to set up unbreakable color blockades.
questions.hintText: The defending bishop controls squares of its own color that the opponent cannot attack.

questions.question: Tactical Motif: What is a 'Windmill' tactic (such as in the famous Torre vs Lasker game)?
questions.optionsString: Spinning the rooks across all 4 corners|A repetitive sequence of discovered checks and regular checks using a Rook and Bishop to win multiple pieces|Promoting three pawns in consecutive turns|A perpetual queen sacrifice
questions.explanation: A windmill uses alternating discovered checks and direct checks with Rook and Bishop to vacuum up the opponent's pieces.
questions.hintText: Discovered check, recapture, discovered check, repeat.

questions.question: Triangulation: What is the purpose of King triangulation in endgames?
questions.optionsString: To move across all three central files|To attack the enemy Queen from three directions|To lose a tempo and return to the original square, transferring the move to the opponent and putting them in zugzwang|To force stalemate
questions.explanation: Triangulation is a 3-move triangular King maneuver that wastes a tempo to hand the turn to the opponent.
questions.hintText: Moving in a triangle to lose a move (tempo) and force the opponent to step away.

questions.question: Queen vs Pawn on 7th Rank: Against which enemy pawns on the 7th rank can a solitary defending King hold a theoretical DRAW against a Queen?
questions.optionsString: Knight and Central pawns (b, d, e, g pawns)|Rook pawns (a, h) and Bishop pawns (c, f)|Only the d-pawn|No pawn can draw against a Queen
questions.explanation: Rook pawns (a, h) and Bishop pawns (c, f) have stalemate resources in the corner, preventing the Queen from winning.
questions.hintText: Stalemate defenses exist on the c, f, a, and h files.

questions.question: Réti Endgame Study: What was Richard Réti's genius concept in his 1921 study featuring a white King chasing two distant pawns?
questions.optionsString: The King moves along a diagonal, simultaneously threatening to support its own passed pawn AND intercept the enemy pawn|Sacrificing the King for a stalemate|Promoting to a bishop|Underpromoting to a knight
questions.explanation: Réti's diagonal King walk exploits Euclidean vs chessboard metric: walking diagonally closes distance to two separate goals simultaneously.
questions.hintText: One diagonal path accomplishes two threats at once.

questions.question: Endgame Mystery: With King, Bishop and wrong-colored Rook pawn (e.g. h-pawn with a dark-squared Bishop where h8 is light), what is the outcome if the enemy King reaches h8?
questions.optionsString: White wins easily|It is a dead theoretical DRAW|Black wins|Loss on time
questions.explanation: The Bishop cannot control the promotion square (h8), allowing the defending King to shuffle between h8 and g8 in unbreakable stalemate.
questions.hintText: The Bishop of the wrong color can never drive the King out of the corner.

questions.question: Checkmating with Minor Pieces: What is the maximum number of moves required to checkmate with Bishop and Knight against a lone King from any position with best play?
questions.explanation: Under optimal play, Bishop and Knight mate can take up to 33 moves to drive the King into the corner matching the Bishop's color.
questions.hintText: Around 33 moves under the W-maneuver technique.

questions.question: Knight Endgames: Which other endgame type are pure Knight and Pawn endgames most mathematically similar to?
questions.optionsString: Rook endgames|Pure King and Pawn endgames|Queen endgames|Bishop endgames
questions.explanation: Because Knights are short-range and cannot lose a tempo, pure Knight endgames closely mirror pure pawn endgames.
questions.hintText: Because knights are short-range pieces that cannot lose a tempo.

questions.question: Tarrasch Rule: What did Siegbert Tarrasch famously state regarding the placement of Rooks in endgames?
questions.optionsString: Rooks belong behind passed pawns — both behind your own to support them, and behind enemy pawns to halt them|Rooks should always stay on the starting rank|Rooks must capture bishops immediately|Rooks must avoid open files
questions.explanation: Tarrasch's rule: Place rooks behind passed pawns to maximize mobility as the pawn advances.
questions.hintText: Behind the passed pawn, whether your own or the opponent's.

questions.question: Rook vs Minor Piece: Can a lone King and Rook force checkmate against a lone King?
questions.optionsString: No, it is a theoretical draw|Only if the King is trapped in the center|Yes, it is a basic fundamental checkmate|Only with pawns present
questions.explanation: King and Rook vs King is an elementary forced checkmate, pushing the King to any edge of the board.
questions.hintText: Box the enemy King to the edge with your Rook and King.

questions.question: Tactical Motif: What is a 'Clearance Sacrifice' in grandmaster play?
questions.optionsString: Sacrificing a piece to clean the entire board|Sacrificing a piece specifically to vacate a square, file, or diagonal for a more deadly attacking piece|Resigning with grace|Trading queens in opening
questions.explanation: A clearance sacrifice frees a vital square or line (e.g. vacating f7 for a queen entry).
questions.hintText: Vacating a square or line to let another piece deliver the blow.

questions.question: Endgame Fortress: What is a 'Fortress' in chess endgames?
questions.optionsString: A defensive setup where the weaker side creates an impenetrable barrier that the opponent cannot break despite material advantage|Surrounding the King with 4 rooks|A double castling structure|A pawn chain stretching from a1 to h8
questions.explanation: A fortress is a theoretical draw where material superiority cannot breach the defensive perimeter.
questions.hintText: An unbreakable defensive wall ensuring a draw despite material deficit.

questions.question: Deflection / Decoy: What is the tactical distinction between 'Deflection' and 'Decoy'?
questions.optionsString: They are exact synonyms with no distinction|Deflection forces a defending piece AWAY from a vital square, while Decoy lures an enemy piece ONTO a fatal square|Decoy is only used with pawns|Deflection only applies to the King
questions.explanation: Deflection removes a defender from duty; decoy pulls a piece onto a doomed square.
questions.hintText: Deflection pushes away from defense; Decoy lures onto a trap.

questions.question: Endgame Studies: In Queen vs Rook endgame (Philidor position), what is the optimal result with best play?
questions.optionsString: Always a draw|Rook always wins|Queen wins by forcing zugzwang and winning the Rook|Loss by repetition
questions.explanation: Queen vs Rook is a forced win for the Queen, though technically demanding to execute without allowing stalemate.
questions.hintText: The Queen and King slowly force the Rook into zugzwang.

questions.question: King Walk / Active King: In the endgame, why does the King transform from a vulnerable target into an aggressive attacking piece?
questions.optionsString: Because check is no longer allowed in endgames|With few pieces remaining, the danger of checkmate drops dramatically, making the King an indispensable active fighter|The King gains the movement powers of a Queen|Pawns protect the King automatically
questions.explanation: As mating material decreases, the King must actively control central squares and assist passed pawns.
questions.hintText: Without queens and heavy pieces, the King cannot easily be checkmated.

questions.question: Intermezzo / Zwischenzug: What is a 'Zwischenzug' in tactical combinations?
questions.optionsString: An 'in-between' unexpected move that changes the tactical evaluation before an expected recapture|Surrendering early|Offering a draw on move 1|A double pawn push
questions.explanation: A Zwischenzug inserts an intermediate threat (like check or counter-attack) before completing the expected line.
questions.hintText: An in-between move inserted before the expected response.

questions.question: Pawn Structure: What is an 'Isolated Pawn' and what is its primary endgame weakness?
questions.optionsString: A pawn with no enemy pawns ahead of it|A pawn with no friendly pawns on adjacent files; it cannot be defended by another pawn and requires piece babysitting|A pawn on the e-file|A pawn that moved three squares
questions.explanation: An isolated pawn cannot be defended by fellow pawns, becoming a chronic target in endgames.
questions.hintText: No neighbor pawns to support it.

questions.question: Overloaded Piece: What does it mean when a piece is 'Overloaded' in tactical calculations?
questions.optionsString: It weighs too much physically|It has moved more than 20 times|It is tasked with defending two critical squares/pieces at the same time and cannot cover both|It is surrounded by 8 pieces
questions.explanation: An overloaded piece has multiple defensive duties; attacking one duty distracts it from the other.
questions.hintText: Trying to guard two things at once.

questions.question: Bishop Pair Advantage: Why is the 'Bishop Pair' generally considered a significant long-term strategic advantage in open positions?
questions.optionsString: Because they can jump over pawns|Together they control both light and dark squares across the entire board, cutting swaths of open diagonals|They can castle together|They promote to two Queens simultaneously
questions.explanation: Two bishops complement each other, covering every square color on open boards where diagonals are clear.
questions.hintText: One covers light, one covers dark — together they dominate open diagonals.

questions.question: Discovered Attack: Why is a discovered check often so devastatingly powerful?
questions.optionsString: The moving piece can attack any target (even a Queen) while the unveiled piece simultaneously checks the King|It counts as two turns in a row|The opponent must surrender their Queen|The King cannot run away
questions.explanation: Because the King MUST respond to the check, the moving piece can capture material with complete impunity.
questions.hintText: The King must deal with the check while the front piece grabs whatever it wants.

questions.question: 7th Rank Rook Infiltration: Why is a Rook invading the 7th rank (the 'Pig on the 7th') so prized in master play?
questions.optionsString: It promotes to Queen immediately|It attacks unmoved enemy pawns horizontally, pins the enemy King to the back rank, and creates deadly mating nets|It prevents all pawn moves|It doubles in value to 10 points
questions.explanation: The 7th rank is the home of vulnerable enemy pawns and clamps down on the enemy King.
questions.hintText: Attacks enemy pawns from the side and traps the King on the 8th rank.
